fet-physics.title: One gate, three drain voltages
fet-physics.prompt: For k = 2 mA/V², VT = 2 V and VGS = 4 V, find drain current at VDS = 0.1, 1 and 3 V.
fet-physics.hint: Find overdrive first, then compare VDS with it.

solution.text: The channel is ohmic while $V_{DS}<u$ and saturated once $V_{DS}\ge u$. So 0.1 V and 1 V are ohmic; 3 V is saturated.

fet-physics.title: Check the tangent
fet-physics.prompt: At ID = 2 mA and overdrive 1 V, find gm and the incremental current for 5 mV input.

solution.text: $I_D=\tfrac12ku^2$, so $g_m=ku=2I_D/u$.
From $I_D=\tfrac12ku^2$, $k=2I_D/u^2$ = 4 mA/V². The extra term is

fet-physics.title: A sloping current source
fet-physics.prompt: The unmodulated saturation current is 2 mA and $\lambda$ = 0.02/V. Find current and ro at VDS = 5 V in the multiplicative model.
fet-physics.hint: Differentiate with respect to drain voltage; keep gate voltage fixed.

solution.answer: 2.2 mA, $r_o$ = 25 kΩ (the shortcut $1/\lambda I_D$ gives 22.7 kΩ).

fet-physics.title: Pinch-off or cutoff?
fet-physics.prompt: At VGS = 3 V, VT = 1 V and VDS = 5 V, is the channel cut off? Explain what happens at its drain end.
fet-physics.hint: Compare overdrive with zero and with drain voltage.

solution.text: The channel pinches off near the drain, but electrons are swept across the high-field region into the drain. Current still flows, set by the gate.

solution.answer: Saturated, not cut off: the drain end is pinched off, but current continues.

fet-physics.title: A current law is not a circuit
fet-physics.prompt: A 12 V supply and 10 kΩ drain resistor feed a source-grounded MOSFET. A saturation-only calculation predicts 2 mA. Is that possible?
fet-physics.hint: Apply KVL before accepting the transistor formula.

solution.text: The drain cannot fall below the grounded source in this circuit, so the saturation answer is impossible.

solution.answer: Not possible: the current is at most 1.2 mA, so the device is in the ohmic region.

jfet-bias.title: A quarter of IDSS
jfet-bias.prompt: For IDSS = 8 mA and VP = −4 V, find VGS and gm at ID = 2 mA.
jfet-bias.hint: Take the physically valid square root.

jfet-bias.title: Design the source resistor
jfet-bias.prompt: Use that same JFET for a 2 mA source with gate at ground. Find RS and approximate minimum drain voltage.
jfet-bias.hint: The source must be above the grounded gate by 2 V.

solution.text: With the gate grounded, $V_S=-V_{GS}$ = 2 V.
Saturation needs $V_{DS}\ge V_{GS}-V_P$ = 2 V.

solution.answer: $R_S$ = 1 kΩ; drain must stay above about 4 V.

jfet-bias.title: A load that is too large
jfet-bias.prompt: Use VDD = 12 V, RD = 5 kΩ, RS = 1 kΩ and the same device. Test the proposed 2 mA bias.

solution.text: 0 V < 2 V, so the 2 mA saturated bias is inconsistent. The real current is lower, with the device in its ohmic region.

solution.answer: Invalid: $V_{DS}$ would be 0 V, below the 2 V saturation requirement.

jfet-bias.title: Degeneration helps a current source
jfet-bias.prompt: With ro = 50 kΩ, gm = 2 mS and RS = 1 kΩ, estimate output resistance.

solution.text: Drive the drain with a test voltage, gate AC-grounded. The source rises by $iR_S$, which reduces $v_{gs}$ and therefore the current.
Source degeneration triples the output resistance of the bare device.

jfet-bias.title: A tiny current through a large resistor
jfet-bias.prompt: A signed gate leakage produces +2 mV gate shift. With gm = 2 mS and RS = 1 kΩ, estimate the resulting current change.
jfet-bias.hint: Source feedback divides the uncorrected change by 1 + gmRS.

jfet-amplifiers.title: Include the next stage
jfet-amplifiers.prompt: gm = 3 mS, RD = 4.7 kΩ, RL = 10 kΩ and RS = 330 Ω. Find gain, ignoring ro.
jfet-amplifiers.hint: First combine the two drain loads.

jfet-amplifiers.title: Almost unity needs a large loop gain
jfet-amplifiers.prompt: A follower has gm = 4 mS and a 2 kΩ effective source load. Find gain and output resistance for a stiff gate drive.
jfet-amplifiers.hint: Use gmR/(1 + gmR) and 1/gm parallel R.

jfet-amplifiers.title: State which output you mean
jfet-amplifiers.prompt: A matched pair has gm = 2 mS per device and RD = 3.3 kΩ. Find one-drain and differential-output gains for differential input.
jfet-amplifiers.hint: Each gate moves by half the differential input.

solution.text: A differential input $v_d$ moves each gate by $\pm v_d/2$.
Its gate moves by $v_d/2$, so its drain current changes by $g_mv_d/2$ and its drain voltage by $-g_mR_Dv_d/2$.
Each drain swings $g_mR_D/2$ = 3.3 per volt of differential input; the two drains swing oppositely, so the difference is twice that.

jfet-amplifiers.title: The gate sees the residual signal
jfet-amplifiers.prompt: For square-law overdrive 2 V, estimate second harmonic ratio at 100 mV peak vgs, and at 25 mV peak.
jfet-amplifiers.hint: Use a/(4u), not the external input when degeneration is present.

solution.text: With $v_{gs}=a\cos\omega t$, $I=\tfrac12k(u+a\cos\omega t)^2$ gives a fundamental of amplitude $kua$ and a second harmonic of amplitude $ka^2/4$.

jfet-amplifiers.title: Cancel the quadratic term
jfet-amplifiers.prompt: Given I = k[(VC + VDS/2 − VT)VDS − VDS²/2], simplify it and find resistance for k = 1 mA/V² and VC − VT = 2 V.

fet-dynamics.title: Zero DC does not mean zero edge current
fet-dynamics.prompt: Estimate current into 20 pF during a 5 V change lasting 10 ns.

solution.answer: About 10 mA during the edge, though the DC gate current is essentially zero.

fet-dynamics.title: A hidden input load
fet-dynamics.prompt: For Av = −10, Cgs = 10 pF, Cgd = 3 pF and source resistance 100 kΩ, estimate input capacitance and pole.
fet-dynamics.hint: The drain moves opposite to the gate.

solution.text: $C_{gd}$ sees $(1-A_v)$ = 11 times the gate swing.

fet-dynamics.title: Frequency is not enough
fet-dynamics.prompt: For R = 10 kΩ and C = 10 nF in an equal-component Wien bridge, find f0 and loop gain when amplifier gain is 2.9.
fet-dynamics.hint: At zero phase the bridge magnitude is one third.

solution.text: At zero phase the Wien network passes one third of its input.

fet-dynamics.title: Check the feedback sign
fet-dynamics.prompt: A noninverting amplifier has RF = 20 kΩ and lower branch 9.5 kΩ plus a JFET. Compare gains at 100 Ω and 500 Ω channel resistance.

solution.text: Higher channel resistance lowers the gain, so making the JFET more resistive as amplitude grows stabilizes the amplitude.

fet-dynamics.title: Account for the divider capacitance
fet-dynamics.prompt: Find the ideal Colpitts tank frequency for L = 100 μH and C1 = C2 = 10 nF.
fet-dynamics.hint: The two capacitors combine in series across the tank.

fet-switches.title: An on-switch attenuates
fet-switches.prompt: Find gain and percentage amplitude error for RON = 100 Ω and RL = 10 kΩ.
fet-switches.hint: Treat the switch as the top resistor of a divider.

fet-switches.title: A 12-bit acquisition interval
fet-switches.prompt: Rsrc = 1 kΩ, RON = 100 Ω, CH = 1 nF. Find time for a full-scale step to settle within half a 12-bit LSB.
fet-switches.hint: Residual fraction must be at most 1/8192.

solution.text: Half an LSB of 12 bits is 1/8192 of full scale.

fet-switches.title: Two separate errors
fet-switches.prompt: A switch deposits 5 pC on 1 nF; total hold leakage is 10 pA. Find initial voltage step and subsequent change over 10 ms.
fet-switches.hint: Use Q/C for the step, It/C for the hold interval.

solution.text: These come from different mechanisms and add (or cancel) according to their polarities.

fet-switches.title: Can one off MOSFET isolate both ways?
fet-switches.prompt: Explain why a single discrete n-channel power MOSFET may conduct with its gate off, and calculate on loss for two back-to-back 20 mΩ devices at 5 A.
fet-switches.hint: Identify the source-to-drain body diode and add both channel resistances.

solution.text: A discrete MOSFET ties its body to the source, forming a diode from source to drain. With the gate off, current can still flow source → drain through it.
Connecting two devices source-to-source puts their diodes in opposition, so one always blocks.

solution.answer: The body diode conducts one way. A back-to-back pair blocks both ways and dissipates 1 W at 5 A.

fet-switches.title: A bipolar signal and a grounded gate
fet-switches.prompt: An n-JFET switch carries signals down to −1 V while its gate is held at 0 V. Why is zero gate voltage not a valid general on command?
fet-switches.hint: All gate voltages are relative to the channel terminals.

solution.text: An n-JFET's gate junction forward-biases above about 0.5 V, so it conducts, injecting current and clamping the signal.
Drive the gate relative to the signal, or keep the signal range where the junction stays reverse biased.

solution.answer: The gate–channel junction would be forward biased by 1 V; 0 V is only 'on' relative to the actual channel voltage.

mosfet-physics.title: A source that moves above the body
mosfet-physics.prompt: VT0 = 1 V, $\gamma$ = 0.5 √V, 2φF = 0.6 V and VSB = 2 V. Find threshold.
mosfet-physics.hint: Use the difference of square roots.

mosfet-physics.title: A fixed gate is not a fixed current
mosfet-physics.prompt: k = 4 mA/V² and VGS = 3 V. Compare saturated currents at VT = 2 V and 2.2 V.
mosfet-physics.hint: Overdrive changes before it is squared.

solution.answer: 2 mA and 1.28 mA: a 0.2 V threshold shift cuts current by 36%.

mosfet-physics.title: Does a 2 V threshold guarantee 3.3 V switching?
mosfet-physics.prompt: A part has a typical 2 V threshold but only specifies on-resistance at 10 V drive. Can you calculate guaranteed 3.3 V conduction loss from that resistance?
mosfet-physics.hint: Threshold is tested at a small current.

solution.text: $V_{th}$ is specified at a tiny current (often 250 µA). It marks the start of conduction, not full enhancement.
It applies only at 10 V of gate drive. At 3.3 V the channel is far less enhanced.
Neither number gives the 3.3 V resistance needed for $P=I^2R_{DS(on)}D$.

solution.answer: No. Choose a part with $R_{DS(on)}$ guaranteed at your gate voltage.

mosfet-physics.title: An exponential decade
mosfet-physics.prompt: At room temperature, assume a subthreshold slope of 90 mV per decade. What gate-voltage increase multiplies current by 1000?
mosfet-physics.hint: A factor of 1000 is three decades.

solution.text: The subthreshold slope is 90 mV per decade.

mosfet-physics.title: A negative threshold
mosfet-physics.prompt: For a depletion MOSFET with k = 2 mA/V² and VT = −2 V, find saturated current at VGS = 0 V and at −1 V.
mosfet-physics.hint: Zero gate voltage still produces positive overdrive.

solution.text: $V_{DS}\ge u$: 2 V and 1 V.

solution.answer: 4 mA at 0 V and 1 mA at −1 V.

mosfet-linear.title: Design the gate divider
mosfet-linear.prompt: A 12 V amplifier needs gate voltage 4 V. Choose a 100 kΩ lower divider resistor; find the upper resistor and divider Thévenin resistance.
mosfet-linear.hint: The lower resistor gets one third of the supply.

mosfet-linear.title: Reference accuracy and heat
mosfet-linear.prompt: Vref = 0.5 V, Rsense = 10 Ω and drain voltage = 10 V. Find current, MOSFET dissipation and current error from +1 mV sense-reference error.
mosfet-linear.hint: The loop holds source voltage near the reference.

solution.text: The loop holds the source at $V_{ref}$.

solution.answer: 50 mA, 0.475 W in the MOSFET, 0.1 mA error.

mosfet-linear.title: Self-bias a normally-on device
mosfet-linear.prompt: For k = 2 mA/V² and VT = −2 V, design a grounded-gate source resistor for 1 mA. Find source and minimum modeled drain voltages.
mosfet-linear.hint: First solve the square law for overdrive.

solution.text: With the gate grounded, $V_S$ = 1 V.

mosfet-linear.title: Current without average load watts
mosfet-linear.prompt: Find peak current for 100 nF driven by a 50 V peak, 1 kHz sine. What happens at 10 kHz?

solution.answer: 31.4 mA at 1 kHz, 314 mA at 10 kHz, with zero average load power.

mosfet-linear.title: A controller consumes the charging current
mosfet-linear.prompt: A 2 mA startup source charges 10 μF from 0 to 12 V while a controller draws a constant 0.5 mA. Find charging time.
mosfet-linear.hint: Only the difference reaches the capacitor.

solution.answer: 80 ms (60 ms without the controller load).

mosfet-power.title: Estimate the plateau interval
mosfet-power.prompt: Drive = 10 V, plateau = 4 V, total gate-path resistance = 20 Ω and Qgd = 12 nC. Estimate gate current and Miller interval.
mosfet-power.hint: Use the voltage across the gate-path resistance.

solution.text: During the plateau the gate sits at 4 V.

mosfet-power.title: Separate the channel and driver
mosfet-power.prompt: 24 V, 5 A, 50% duty, hot resistance 24 mΩ, total overlap 50 ns and 100 kHz. Qg = 30 nC at 10 V. Find three power terms.
mosfet-power.hint: Conduction uses duty; overlap and gate energy occur per cycle.

solution.text: During each transition V and I overlap roughly linearly, which gives a factor of ½.

solution.answer: 0.30 W conduction, 0.30 W overlap, 0.03 W gate drive (mostly in the driver).

mosfet-power.title: Close the temperature loop
mosfet-power.prompt: Assume TA = 40°C, thermal resistance 50°C/W, fixed switching loss 0.3 W and conduction loss 0.25[1 + 0.004(TJ − 25)] W. Solve TJ self-consistently.
mosfet-power.hint: Substitute the power expression into TJ = TA + RθP.

mosfet-power.title: A faster clamp
mosfet-power.prompt: A 10 mH inductor carries 2 A. Find stored energy and ideal decay time with 24 V opposing clamp voltage, neglecting winding resistance.

mosfet-power.title: A small inductance makes a large voltage
mosfet-power.prompt: Find source bounce across 5 nH for di/dt = 1 A/ns. Explain why the driver reference matters.
mosfet-power.hint: Use v = L di/dt with SI units.

solution.text: If the driver returns to a ground beyond that inductance, the 5 V subtracts from the gate drive. A Kelvin source connection avoids sharing the power path.

solution.answer: 5 V of source bounce, which directly changes $V_{GS}$.

power-fet-circuits.title: Size for charge demand
power-fet-circuits.prompt: A high-side event uses 30 nC gate charge plus 20 nC of other charge. Find ideal minimum bootstrap capacitance for 0.5 V droop.

solution.answer: At least 100 nF, before derating margin.

power-fet-circuits.title: Volt-seconds and ripple
power-fet-circuits.prompt: An ideal buck converts 24 V to 12 V at 100 kHz using 100 μH. Find duty and inductor ripple.
power-fet-circuits.hint: Set average inductor voltage to zero.

power-fet-circuits.title: Where the supply energy goes
power-fet-circuits.prompt: Charge 1000 μF to 24 V with a 1 A linear limiter and no load. Find time, stored energy and pass-device energy.
power-fet-circuits.hint: Integrate capacitor current and pass-device power.

solution.text: The supply delivers 1 A at 24 V for 24 ms.

solution.answer: 24 ms; 0.288 J stored and 0.288 J in the pass device.

power-fet-circuits.title: Count both intervals
power-fet-circuits.prompt: For 5 A, diode drop 0.8 V, two 100 ns dead intervals each cycle and 100 kHz, estimate dead-time conduction loss.
power-fet-circuits.hint: Multiply diode power by the total fraction of time.

power-fet-circuits.title: Convert switching energy to heat
power-fet-circuits.prompt: An IGBT has 1.8 V on drop at 10 A, 50% duty and 0.6 mJ total switching energy per cycle. Find total of these losses at 20 kHz.
power-fet-circuits.hint: Conduction is voltage times current times duty.

parallel-mosfets.title: Unequal channels
parallel-mosfets.prompt: Two fully enhanced MOSFETs of 20 and 30 mΩ share 20 A. Find currents and channel losses.
parallel-mosfets.hint: Both branches see the same voltage.

parallel-mosfets.title: Heat one branch
parallel-mosfets.prompt: The 20 mΩ device warms from 25 to 100°C with $\alpha$ = 0.004/°C. The other stays at 30 mΩ. Recalculate sharing at 20 A.

solution.text: Current moves away from the hot device: positive tempco gives self-balancing.

parallel-mosfets.title: Individual feedback matters
parallel-mosfets.prompt: gm = 2 S and threshold shift = −50 mV. Compare small current changes with source resistance 0 and 0.5 Ω at fixed common gate voltage.

solution.text: Each branch needs its own resistor; a shared one senses only the total.

parallel-mosfets.title: An equilibrium can be unstable
parallel-mosfets.prompt: For a lumped thermal model with Rθ = 10°C/W, evaluate stability when dP/dT is 0.15 W/°C, and when it is 0.04 W/°C.

solution.text: Heating rises faster than cooling: a small warm-up creates more heat than it removes, so the temperature runs away.
Cooling wins, so perturbations decay.

solution.answer: 0.15 W/°C: unstable; 0.04 W/°C: stable (in this lumped model).

parallel-mosfets.title: Competing temperature effects
parallel-mosfets.prompt: Assume fractional k slope −0.004/°C and threshold slope −0.002 V/°C. Find fractional current slope at overdrives 0.5 and 2 V.
parallel-mosfets.hint: Differentiate the square law at fixed gate voltage.

solution.text: $I=\tfrac12ku^2$ with $u=V_{GS}-V_T$ and $V_{GS}$ fixed.
